purpose: Non-authoritative evidence-to-requirement suggestions for one exact Shine Defence review checklist.
binding: The suggestion artifact binds to one exact candidate id, release/profile identity, checklist generation timestamp and canonical registry blob.
Suggestions are derived only from the candidate evidence already copied into the canonical checklist and the exact checklist requirement text.
Suggestion generation never changes checklist item state, evidenceRefs, reviewer notes, humanAuthorization, candidate status, certification receipt, reviewed ledger or review decision.

confidence.meaning: Strong lexical/topic overlap between the requirement and candidate evidence; still requires human confirmation.
Meaningful but incomplete overlap; reviewer should inspect the evidence before using it.
Weak contextual overlap; surfaced only as a possible lead.

rules: Each checklist requirement receives zero or more ranked evidence suggestions and an explicit evidenceGap boolean.
A suggestion must reference an evidence id present in the canonical checklist and an item id present in that same checklist.
Scores are deterministic numeric heuristics from 0 to 1; they are not probabilities or security verdicts.
At most three evidence suggestions are retained per checklist item.
Matched terms and evidence metadata used in the heuristic are recorded so the reviewer can understand why a suggestion appeared.
A requirement with no retained suggestion has evidenceGap=true.
A requirement with one or more retained suggestions has evidenceGap=false.
Suggestions never mark a requirement satisfied and never authorize approval.
The review workspace or human reviewer must explicitly confirm any evidence mapping before it becomes part of the canonical checklist.
Suggestion artifacts fail closed on candidate, checklist, registry or evidence drift.
nonClaims: A high-confidence suggestion does not prove a requirement is satisfied.
The heuristic does not understand source code, deployment state or external evidence beyond the bounded evidence metadata supplied to the candidate.
No score is a probability of safety, correctness or certification success.
The evidence assistant cannot approve, reject, certify or revoke a release.
